scope: Read-only review of exactly five iOS import-drain delta paths; no Swift/compiler/runtime execution
priorFinding: A cancelled/departed view lost the only provider task handle and could start another original read before the prior provider settled.
reviewedCorrection: Synchronous MainActor admission increments a two-operation bound before suspension; only the cancellable waiter is returned, not the retained worker.

Private unstructured worker waits for the prior worker, then awaits the full operation and decrements capacity only after completion; losing/cancelling the view waiter cannot release the drain barrier.
The static shared queue is used by both picker preparation and actual read; a replacement view uses the same lane.
Queued operations check the captured readID and ticket before popping PhotosPicker items/URLs; cancellation clears the bounded view queue and stale queued closures return without opening providers.
An active import awaits loadTransferable/FileRepresentation completion or detached Files read; stale results are checked and discarded before its operation returns and the successor starts.
FileRepresentation retains its system URL within the importing closure while awaiting detached bounded file I/O; File/NSFileCoordinator work is not executed synchronously on MainActor.

No obvious Swift5/minimal-concurrency type or actor-isolation incompatibility was found by reading Task<Void,Never>, MainActor closure signatures, Sendable media DTO and detached URL/data handoff; this is not compilation proof.
Three authored regressions use synchronous queue admission and a delayed provider gate for cancel/reselect, two screen-owned models and overflow; the fixture boundary is explicit.
limitation: An uncooperative provider can keep the one active slot occupied; current source intentionally waits and reports busy rather than admitting another original. Actual platform scheduling/lifetime still needs Xcode/device evidence.
